Okay, so I need to figure out which statement about rocks is true. The options are A) Minerals are made of rocks, B) Crystals are made of rocks, C) Rocks are made of one or more minerals, and D) Magma is made of solid rock. 

First, I remember that rocks are made up of minerals. So, option C seems correct because it says rocks are made of one or more minerals. But wait, I also recall that some rocks, like obsidian, are made from cooled magma, which doesn't contain minerals. So maybe C isn't always true. 

Looking at the other options, A says minerals are made of rocks, which doesn't make sense because minerals are the building blocks of rocks, not the other way around. B says crystals are made of rocks, but crystals are actually a type of mineral, so that's also incorrect. 

D says magma is made of solid rock, but magma is molten, so it's not solid. Magma can have crystals and other materials suspended in it, but it's not made of solid rock. So D is true. 

Wait, but the initial analysis said C was correct. Maybe I need to double-check. Rocks are generally made of minerals, but some rocks, like coal, are organic and not minerals. So C isn't universally true. Therefore, the correct answer should be D because it's always true, whereas C has exceptions. 

So the mistake was in thinking that C was correct without considering the exceptions. The agent didn't account for all types of rocks, leading to an incorrect conclusion.
</think>
